label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: I have NEWS (the good kind)

Ok. Deep breath. I've started this post like six times.

I'm going out on my own. As of October 22 there is a real, filed, official business called Fernhollow Photo LLC, and it's mine!!

Here's how it happened. Marisol closed Rosebud Lane at the end of October. She told me on October 6, and after four years of shooting for her I'm not going to pretend that wasn't a lot to take in. But in the same breath she told me she was already sending 2027 couples my way, and that she thought I'd been ready to do this for a while.

And honestly? I've been planning this in my head for about two years. I just never said it out loud, because saying it out loud makes it real. So no, I didn't panic and grab the nearest idea. I already wanted this. It just showed up sooner than I'd scheduled it.

Now, for the worriers (hi Dad), here's where things actually stand:

I have 14 weddings booked for 2027 already. Six of those are Marisol's referrals and eight are couples who found me completely on their own. June is the busiest month with four, and the furthest one out is at Wallowa Lake in September, which I'm already way too excited about.

The website went live November 1. It's real, you can go look at it, there's a contact form and everything.

Jae is going to second shoot the big weddings with me. He gets paid per wedding, so I'm not doing a 200 person reception alone and I'm also not running a payroll.

And DAD. Health insurance. It's handled. I picked a marketplace plan on November 5 and it starts January 1. I read your comment back in August about steady hours, health insurance, and no knees involved. I can give you one out of three. The knees are staying involved, sorry. I know the speech comes from love, and you can still give it at Ruthie's if you really want to, but I'll have answers this time.

Ok, the fun stuff.

My first booking that was 100% mine, no referral, is a couple named Dahlia and Ken. They're getting married June 12 at Timberline. They found me because of the photos I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls, and that's what sold them. They said yes earlier this month and I read the email about four times before I believed it. Somebody looked at my pictures and decided they wanted me at their wedding. That's the whole job and it still got me.

I filed the LLC paperwork on my lunch break, on my phone, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. Very glamorous. I hit submit and then I cried a little, in the parking lot, next to a cart return. Then I went in and bought a sandwich.

Sam made me a cake that night. It was supposed to say FERNHOLLOW. It said FERNHOLOW. He noticed about one second after I did and the look on his face was the best part of my whole week. We ate it anyway. It was really good.

About the name. Grandma, this part is for you. Fernhollow is the trail behind your old place in Gresham, the one with all the ferns down in the dip where it's always a little bit wet. That's where I took my first real pictures, with your Pentax, when you showed me how to load the film and told me to quit shooting everything and wait for something worth it. I've been waiting for something worth it ever since. I wanted the business to be named after where it started, and it started with you. So every time somebody books me, your trail is on the invoice.

And I have to say something about Marisol, because I wouldn't be doing any of this without her. She basically taught me everything. How to run a wedding day without anybody noticing you're running it. How to get a nervous groom to stop standing like he's in a lineup. How to keep shooting when it rains, when the timeline falls apart, when the flower girl takes off with your lens cap. Four years of that. Then she turned around and handed six of her couples to me and told them I was the one. I don't know how you thank somebody for that, but I'm going to try for a very long time.

Is it scary? Yeah. It's scary. I'm not going to act like it isn't. There's no boss now, and nobody's deciding my calendar or my paycheck but me. Some mornings I think that's the best thing I've ever heard, and some mornings I have to go walk Pickle around the block twice. But I have a plan and I have bookings. Sam is all in, even if he can't spell it, and I've got Jae for the big days. I've also got four years of doing this job really, really well for someone else. I'm ready to do it with my own name on it. Well, Grandma's trail's name.

So here's what I'd love from you guys. Be excited with me! Ask me about it at Thanksgiving, I want to talk about it. I just didn't want it coming out for the first time over the turkey with everybody's forks in the air.

Also, I'm bringing the camera to Ruthie's. If anybody wants free family pictures while we're all in one place and wearing real clothes, I'm offering. Couples, kids, the cousins, whoever. Comment and tell me and I'll plan for it. Uncle Greg, I promise it'll be faster than Christmas. Bree, I know you said visitors after Thanksgiving, so whenever you're ready, Juniper gets her own shoot. I will wash my hands a lot.

Mom, yes, Sam's coming. We're bringing rolls and the cranberry thing.

Love you all so much. See you on the 26th.

Tessa
(owner of Fernhollow Photo, which I'm still getting used to typing)
